      <title>Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/29/brazil-victory-planet-democracy-lessons-lula-win</link>
      <description><p>The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France</p><p></p><p>Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France.</p><p>The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/29/brazil-victory-planet-democracy-lessons-lula-win">Continue reading...</a></description>
